text:
The Marisol Trench probe reached 9,400 metres, the deepest descent yet logged by Seastone Instruments, according to a company statement released Tuesday. The autonomous craft spent 14 hours underwater before surfacing with intact sensor packs and a full pressure sample set. Seastone said the run beat its prior internal target by 1,100 metres and cut expected drill-validation costs by 18%.

Project lead Irena Volkov said the data should help refine sub-sea mapping systems ahead of commercial deployments next year. Investors took notice: shares in the privately held supplier’s listed partner, Northglass Marine, rose 4.2% in afternoon trading. For the sector, the result signals faster qualification cycles for ultra-deepwater equipment and could tighten competition among trench-exploration vendors.
